title: Audition spectral palette and typographic rhythm for dense tables
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Dense datagrids and compact tables in our product surface suffer from visual noise and inconsistent affordances across themes. Current token ramps were tuned for mid-density surfaces; when used in compact tables they either lose contrast or create distracting high-contrast seams. This ticket is an audition exercise to explore a spectral color ramp and adjusted typographic rhythm that preserves legibility, row separation, and interaction affordances at high density.

Scope: Create a small, testable token subset (primary/secondary surface colors, subtle separators, two compact type tiers, and a micro-elevation ladder) and validate in 3 representative table patterns (list view, dense datagrid with horizontal stripe, and inline editable grid). Deliver candidate tokens, Figma kit, accessibility report, and recommendation for rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Three candidate spectral palettes delivered as token files (JSON) and Figma styles
Compact typography scale defined (compact-body, compact-caption) with specs for line-height and truncation behavior
Separator and micro-elevation ladder tuned so row separation remains visible at 72/120/200ppi and across light/dark themes
Contrast report demonstrating WCAG AA for primary body text and AA/large for secondary text across candidate palettes
Usability notes from at least two PM/Eng partners after prototype validation in a staging dashboard
Proposal for migration strategy that includes opt-in flag, canary cohort, and revert path
design_notes: Strategy: avoid making denser surfaces darker overall; instead increase perceived separation via subtle chroma shifts and a 1-2 step micro-elevation scale to keep shadows minimal but directional
Spectral approach: use a neutral-gray anchor then introduce +/- chroma offsets on surface and separator tokens so selection states read reliably without raising base luminance
Typography: compact-body at 13px/18px line-height; compact-caption at 11px/14px. Use tighter letter-spacing and explicit truncation rules for inline editable cells
Interaction states: test focus rings at 2px with blended overlay rather than solid stroke to reduce visual clutter in dense rows
Device/scale tests: include 1x (desktop), 1.5x (high-dpi laptops), and 2x (retina) in Figma frames; export PNGs for pixel-level review
decisions: Will keep base semantic tokens unchanged for general surfaces; create a "compact.*" token namespace for table-specific overrides
Favor a 2-step micro-elevation (compact-elev-0, compact-elev-1) instead of a large multi-step ladder to avoid stacking artifacts
Prototype will ship as experimental token set behind feature-flag and not overwrite global tokens until validated
Accessibility thresholds: primary body must meet AA (4.5:1) and captions should meet AA large (3:1) when possible; document tradeoffs where not achievable
comments: 2025-03-13 - Ava Chen: Started exploratory Figma frames. Trying three chroma offsets: cool-lean, warm-lean, neutral. Initial preference leans neutral for enterprise dashboards.
2025-03-15 - Diego Martinez (Engineering): Noted that compact-elev-1 shadows add GPU rasterization cost on WebGL rendering in one legacy table. Suggest testing a flat overlay variant.
2025-03-19 - Priya Nair (Creator): Ran contrast matrix. Warm-lean failed AA for caption in dark theme; removing warm palette from candidate list.
2025-03-22 - PM Review (Elena Ortiz): Asked for migration plan and clear rollback path; requested additional measurement of token size impact on bundle.
2025-03-26 - Ava Chen: Updated Figma kit with truncation tokens and exported accessibility screenshots for review. Preparing handoff to ENG for staging integration.
